findings.title: Vector ids are not unique across tenants in a shared store
findings.detail: The backend names a chunk `<tenant>-<key>-<n>` and upserts on that id. With slugs `acme` and `acme-corp`, acme's `corp-collide.txt` and acme-corp's `collide.txt` get the same id `acme-corp-collide.txt-0`; acme's reindex took the row over (now acme, holding acme's text), and acme-corp lost its document. Integrity, not confidentiality: the row moves with its tenant column, so neither tenant reads the other's text. Not reachable on the platform, where each tenant has its own store and docs-signer keys start with a UUID; it matters only if stores were ever shared.

findings.title: Within one tenant: a caller-chosen prefix empties the tenant's own index
findings.detail: `/api/index` in this image takes `prefix` from the request body; a prefix matching nothing found no documents, and the resync's purge then deleted every one of the tenant's chunks (4 → 0 in the shared layout, 4 → 0 in the separate layout). The other tenant's rows were untouched. /api/index is public, so anyone can do this to any tenant; a reindex restores it. The backend working copy no longer reads the prefix from the body (uncommitted, not in this image).

findings.title: Within one tenant: top_k is unbounded
findings.detail: `AskRequest.top_k` has no upper bound, and one request with top_k 10000 returned every chunk that cleared the relevance gate (3 of 4 for acme, 5 of 5 for acme-corp), all the tenant's own. Not a cross-tenant leak, but any visitor of the public chatbot can pull as much of a knowledge base into one prompt as clears the gate.

findings.title: Developer files shipped in the backend image
findings.detail: `/app/.env.local` (1392 bytes, sets VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN; a token from https://oidc.vercel.com/kaltrina127316s-projects that expired 2026-09-13T22:11:22.000Z), `/app/.vercel/project.json` (124 bytes), `/app/.vercel/README.txt` (520 bytes). The backend's .dockerignore excludes `.env` but not `.env.local` or `.vercel/`, and the platform copies the same image into every customer's registry, so each customer receives them.
